title: Q-Block Computing Establishes Ottawa Headquarters to Expand Quantum Hardware R&D - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Canadian quantum systems developer Q-Block Computing has set up its headquarters in an Ottawa facility near federal defense and research institutions while keeping manufacturing in Alberta, and is recruiting technical staff. It targets defense, telecom security and critical infrastructure with three atomic and photonic platforms.

insights.claim: Q-Block Computing has acquired an operational facility at 20 Colonnade Road in Ottawa as corporate headquarters, centralizing research, optical and systems engineering and administration near federal defense and research institutions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Co-locating with government customers signals a defense-led go-to-market.
insights.locator: Canadian quantum systems developer Q-Block Computing

insights.claim: Manufacturing and assembly stay in Alberta, with Ottawa handling prototype design and software development in Ontario and device fabrication lines in Alberta.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Two-site structure splits R&D and production across provinces.

insights.claim: Q-Block has opened technical recruitment across quantum physics, digital-analog electrical design, FPGA development and photonic packaging.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hiring areas suggest focus on engineering deployable systems rather than pure research.

insights.claim: Q-Block develops three platforms: AllanQ for precision timing and frequency standards in GNSS-denied environments, LuciaQ for secure photonic networking, and PolarisQ for quantum information processing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Product lines map to near-term sensing, timing and secure-communication demand rather than computing.

insights.claim: The systems target operational integration across defense, telecommunications security and critical infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions quantum timing and networking as national-security-adjacent procurement.
